note: Owner-requested log of Analyze-tab recommendations, captured at the moment the call was read, so it can be graded later against what actually happened. Append-only: never rewrite a call's `call`/`levels`/`context` block after logging (the whole point is that the record predates the outcome). Only `review.status` and `outcome` are ever filled in.

calls.loggedBy: owner request (screenshot of the Analyze Recommendation card)

call.headline: Uptrend with room left to the first resistance.
call.why: price is above the 50-day average, and RSI 54 - mid-range
call.engineWarning: The targets don't pay for the risk here - the first target is only 0.70x the distance to the stop. Wait for a better entry (or a target that clears it) rather than sizing up.
call.note: azCore's raw state was Buy Opportunity; the sub-1.5 reward:risk is what downgraded it to ACCUMULATE (v141 rule).

levelProvenance.stop: the -10% clamp ceiling (2xATR/swing-low was wider than the clamp on a ~100%-vol name)
levelProvenance.target2: the all-time high off hist.month (76.87) - not a 6-week objective

levels.invalidates: a daily close under 39.47 flips the call to Caution

indicators.flowDetail: revision 6.7 (consensus improving +0.09 over 3mo, 23 analysts); surprise 4.61 (2/4 beats, avg -1.1%); no insider/award coverage

measuredEdge.verdictAtCallTime: this state HAS NOT been paying lately - the app marked its own call down for it

context.shortCallOverlay: three short $50 calls expiring 2026-09-11 marked at $0.005 - i.e. expiring worthless that same day, so the covered-call cap on upside lifts right as this call is made
context.materialTension: an ACCUMULATE on a name that is already 78% of equity in a ~2x levered book. Under the v125 self-directed mandate concentration is advisory-only (deliberate gamble account), so this is not a rule breach - but it is the fact most worth judging the call against.

review.horizonRationale: 6 weeks = the far edge of the call's own stated 2-6 week swing horizon, and inside pickgrade's 60-day GRADE_HORIZON_DAYS.
questions: Path, on a CLOSING basis and in order: did a close clear target1 (46.93) before a close broke the stop (39.47), or the reverse? If a single bar spans both, the stop is tested first (pickgrade's rule).
Excursion: max favourable and max adverse move from 43.85 over the window, with dates. A call can be 'right' and still have been untradeable through the drawdown.

Base-rate calibration - the single most valuable answer here: the app predicted its own 'Buy Opportunity' state would average -0.33% over 20 sessions and -1.88pp vs SPY. What did IREN actually do over its next 20 sessions, and over the full 6 weeks, absolute and vs SPY? Did the self-measurement earn its keep?
R:R honesty: the card warned the targets don't pay (0.70:1). Even on a favourable outcome, did the realised move pay for a 10% stop? Was the warning the most useful line on the card?

Stop realism: -10% was the clamp CEILING on a ~100%-vol name. Did price whipsaw through 39.47 and recover? If so, the clamp - not the analysis - decided the outcome, and that is a code finding, not a market finding.
Confidence calibration: 64% after a -10 haircut. Over the app's logged calls so far, is 64% distinguishable from a coin toss? (n=1 here - record the datapoint, do not conclude from it.)
Fundamentals: scored 28/100. Over 6 weeks, did that matter at all, or is the fundamentals input just noise at a swing horizon on this kind of name?

Position context: would ACTING on this (adding to a name already at 78% of equity on ~2x leverage) have been prudent regardless of whether the direction was right? Separate 'was the call correct' from 'was the call actionable for THIS book'.
Did the short-$50-call expiry on 2026-09-11 change the picture - i.e. was the upside actually available this time in a way it had not been while the calls were on?
review.outputContract: Fill `outcome` below, set status to 'graded', keep every field above byte-identical, and push. A grade that quietly edits the original call is worthless.
